findings.current: everyone—ally and enemy alike—thought the Blood Lord was dead.
findings.defect: The Korean says everyone thought of the Blood Lord’s death, not that everyone believed he was already dead. The translation makes their reaction more certain.
findings.rationale: “혈주의 죽음을 떠올리지 않았던 이는 없었다” means no one failed to think of his death; it does not state that they concluded he was dead.
findings.replacement: there wasn’t a single person—ally or enemy—who hadn’t thought of the Blood Lord’s death.

findings.current: It was well beyond what he and the other allies had expected.
findings.defect: This retains the comparison to their expectations but omits the source’s separate observation that the scene was indescribably bizarre and the recovery astonishingly fast.
findings.rationale: The Korean explicitly describes both the strangeness of the scene and the speed of the recovery before saying it exceeded what the allies had expected.
findings.replacement: It was a sight too bizarre to describe—and a recovery far too fast, well beyond what he and the other allies had expected.

summary: Two minor fidelity defects: the opening turns thoughts of the Blood Lord’s death into certainty that he was dead, and a description of the recovery as bizarre and too fast is omitted.
